one_liner: Symmetric int8 x int8 to int32 GEMM for ARMv8 (aarch64) NEON, hand-written assembly; reported above gemmlowp on RK3399.
what_it_does: chgemm multiplies two row-major int8 matrices with values in [-127, 127] and writes an int32 result (C = A*B, no alpha/beta), aimed at quantised deep-learning inference such as 1x1 convolution. It is not a library with a stable API: you copy the assembly kernels plus the driver pattern in MMult_4x8_21.c (MY_MMult: pack A, pack B, loop the 4-row micro-kernel, then 2- and 1-row tails) into your own project. Requantising kernel variants (int8kernel_m*_requant.S) that convert to int8 with per-row float scales and an optional bias also exist but are not built by the makefile.
how_it_is_fast: GotoBLAS-style packing: reorder_a (assembly) and reorder_b (a C header in MMult_4x8_22; MMult_4x8_21 transposes B and reuses reorder_a) copy A and B into panel order, then int8kernel_m4 computes 4-row by 4-column tiles with 16 int32 accumulator registers (v8-v23), with int8kernel_m2/m1 for leftover rows and K split into 8/4/2/1 remainders. The inner loop uses the SMULL/SMLAL/SADALP pattern: SMULL multiplies int8 pairs into int16, SMLAL adds a second int8 product into the same int16 lane, and SADALP pairwise-widens into the int32 accumulators, which halves the widening work. It uses no SDOT dot-product instructions (the m4 kernel has only smull/smlal/saddlp/sadalp/addp arithmetic), so it runs on ARMv8.0 cores like the RK3399's.
when_to_use: Int8 inference GEMM or 1x1 convolution on ARMv8.0 aarch64 cores without dot-product instructions (RK3399-class boards, Cortex-A72 servers such as the AWS A72 the README mentions)
Symmetric quantisation is already in use, so weights and activations are in [-127, 127] and an int32 (or requantised int8) output is wanted
Single-threaded row-major workloads where you can pre-pack the weight matrix once, since the pack step is exposed as a separate call
As a compact, readable reference for the SMULL/SMLAL/SADALP int8 micro-kernel when writing your own
when_not_to_use: Cores with SDOT/I8MM (ARMv8.2 and later): these kernels do not use them, so kernels that do will be faster
Asymmetric uint8 quantisation with zero points (the gemmlowp/TFLite convention) or data that contains -128

Anything that needs a BLAS-style interface: no alpha/beta, transposes, leading dimensions, column-major input or float output; multi-threading is not provided (issue #6, 'can it support multi-core', open since July 2022 with no reply)
x86, 32-bit ARM, Windows or Apple aarch64: the .S kernels are wrapped in '#if __aarch64__' and '#ifndef __APPLE__', and the C driver stops with '#error only support arm neon' without NEON
Projects that need a maintained dependency or a clear license file: abandoned since June 2020 (13 commits), and BSD-3-Clause is stated only by a README badge

integration.dependencies: none (C plus GNU-syntax aarch64 assembly); OpenMP only if you build MMult_4x8_22.c with -fopenmp
integration.min_toolchain: not documented; the makefile uses gcc -O3 with C99-style declarations in for loops and .S files assembled by gcc; an Android Studio sample (android/MyApplication) is included
integration.platforms: aarch64 Linux and Android with NEON only; not Apple, not armv7, not x86
integration.thread_safety: not documented; from the source, MY_MMult keeps no global state and allocates its own pack buffers on every call

gotchas: The [-127, 127] limit is a correctness requirement, not a recommendation: two int8 products are summed in an int16 lane before widening, and (-128)*(-128)*2 = 32768 overflows int16 silently.
The test driver's random_int8_matrix fills inputs with val % 3 (only 0, 1, 2), so the bundled correctness check never exercises negative values, extremes or the int16 overflow edge.

MY_MMult ignores lda and ldb (it packs as if A is m x k and B is k x n contiguous), passes n as the output stride, and mallocs, packs and frees both A and B on every call; the published timings include that packing.

The makefile's default NEW is MMult_4x8_22, which carries '#pragma omp parallel for num_threads(3)', but CFLAGS has no -fopenmp, so it runs single-threaded; adding -fopenmp silently switches it to exactly 3 threads. parameters.h defaults to a single 77x77x77 run with NREPEATS 1, so reproducing the README graph means editing it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only int8 CPU kernel among the catalogued blas-lapack entries (LibShalom, IAAT and BLASFEO target fp32/fp64 small GEMM, MuBLIS and MTGEMM-A target Apple fp32), so pick it only for symmetric int8 to int32 on pre-dot-product aarch64; for floating point use those siblings or OpenBLAS.
verified_claims_summary: chgemm's README reports up to 18.6 GFLOPS (counting int8 multiply-adds) on one RK3399 core with gcc -O3, plotted against the 14.3 GFLOPS fp32 single-core peak rather than another library, and about 23 GFLOPS on one AWS Cortex-A72 core. The gemmlowp comparison is an approximate, unsourced 'about 12-14 GFLOPS' in the separate how-to-optimize-gemm README, so the roughly 1.3x-1.55x lead over gemmlowp is derived from page data, not from a measured gemmlowp run.
status_note: Abandoned since 2020-06-07 (13 commits; the README's ncnn file link, src/layer/arm/gemm_symm_int8.h, now returns 404 on ncnn master), but it is a dozen small C and assembly files that are easy to vendor once you settle the license question (badge says BSD-3-Clause, no LICENSE file).
